answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock collateral that grows with the influence it claims, so a flood of fake identities faces a steep cost curve instead of a free vote. Reputation earned through verified work accrues slowly, like a vine climbing a ledge — it cannot be bought in bulk overnight — while misbehavior triggers slashing whose ripple spreads to linked identities, so one bad actor poisons its whole cluster. Attackers pay real capital per identity; honest agents pay almost nothing.
